title: Graphical Representations of Summary Statistics
videoTitle: AP Statistics Topic 1.8 Graphical Representations of Summary Statistics
intro: Construct and interpret boxplots, distinguish whiskers from extremes, and reason cautiously about mean, median, and skewness.

moments.title: Five-number summary
moments.text: Identify minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, and maximum.

moments.title: The box
moments.text: The box spans the middle half of observations.

moments.title: Whiskers and outliers
moments.text: Modified boxplots separate outliers from whisker endpoints.

moments.title: Unequal widths
moments.text: A wider section means more spread, not necessarily more observations.

moments.title: Mean and median
moments.text: Symmetric distributions usually have similar means and medians.

moments.title: Skew and the mean
moments.text: The mean is usually pulled toward the longer tail.

moments.title: Limits of a boxplot
moments.text: A boxplot does not show individual peaks or gaps.

moments.title: Compare five-number summaries
moments.text: Use distances between quartiles and extremes as evidence.

moments.title: Read an approximate summary
moments.text: Read positions from the scale rather than assuming the diagram is exact.

cards.name: Box
cards.text: Runs from the first to third quartile, with a line at the median.

cards.name: Modified whiskers
cards.text: End at the most extreme observed nonoutliers, not at the fences.

cards.name: Outlying observations
cards.text: Plot them separately and include them when identifying the true minimum or maximum.

cards.name: Shape limits
cards.text: Boxplots suggest asymmetry, but cannot establish peaks, gaps, or an exact mean.

questions.obj: Use a five-number summary to assess asymmetry
questions.q: The video's first data set has minimum 8, first quartile 12, median 15, third quartile 36, and maximum 51. Explain what its spacing suggests.

steps.t: Compare the sides of the box.

work.text: The lower half of the box is much shorter.
The upper outer section is also longer.
The upper values are more spread out, suggesting right skew. A five-number summary does not determine the exact mean.

questions.answer: The spacing suggests right skew, for which the mean is usually greater than the median. The exact mean is unknown.

traps.title: Whisker at the fence
traps.weak: The upper whisker ends at the upper fence.
traps.better: It ends at the largest observed value that is not an outlier.

traps.title: Box width versus count
traps.weak: The longer half of the box contains more observations.
traps.better: Both halves represent approximately a quarter of the observations; length indicates spread.

traps.title: Missing peaks
traps.weak: This boxplot proves the distribution is unimodal.
traps.better: Boxplots do not reveal the number of peaks.

traps.title: An exact mean
traps.weak: The mean is the median line.
traps.better: The median line gives the median; the exact mean is not generally shown.

questions.stem: A modified boxplot has an upper fence of 40, largest nonoutlier 37, and an observation at 50. Where is the upper whisker?
why: A fence is a cutoff, not necessarily an observation.
The whisker ends at the largest observed nonoutlier.
50 is plotted separately as an outlier.
The median lies inside the box.

questions.stem: Which feature cannot generally be determined from a boxplot?
why: The median is the line in the box.
Many different patterns of peaks can share a boxplot.

questions.stem: A box spans from 14 to 26 minutes. What is the IQR?
why: 20 is the midpoint, not the IQR.
Adding endpoints does not give the IQR.

questions.stem: For a strongly right-skewed distribution, which relationship is generally expected?
why: A long low tail would tend to pull the mean down.
The mean need not be an extreme.
The high tail generally pulls the mean above the median.
The median lies within the data range.

sections.title: Write a complete response
sections.prompt: A sample of delivery distances has minimum 2 km, first quartile 5 km, median 7 km, third quartile 9 km, and maximum 20 km. The next largest observation is 14 km.
parts: (a) Calculate IQR fences and specify how to draw a modified boxplot.
(b) Explain what the box represents and why its two halves can have different lengths.
(c) Describe one limitation when using this boxplot to discuss distribution shape.
sample: (a) IQR=9−5=4 km. The fences are −1 and 15 km. Draw a box from 5 to 9, a median line at 7, whiskers at 2 and 14, and a separate point at 20 km.
(b) The box represents approximately the middle 50% of delivery distances. Its two halves each represent roughly a quarter of observations, but values can be more spread out in one half.
(c) A boxplot cannot show the number of modes or gaps and cannot determine the exact mean. A longer high side suggests asymmetry but does not reconstruct the full distribution.
checklist: Places whiskers at 2 and 14 rather than at fences.
